title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named University of Iowa destinations with documented uses for studying, gathering, cultural activity, and recreation.

cards.title: Set up a shared work session
cards.subtitle: Main Library, first floor
cards.notes: Reserve a group room through Office 365 or in person, then use its monitor and writeable glass to keep a project visible to everyone.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor collaboration hub with reservable rooms and open group areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The Learning Commons has 22 student-reservable group spaces, including private rooms and open areas with writing surfaces and laptop-connectable monitors.
cards.source_title: Group Spaces | University of Iowa Libraries
cards.access_notes: Student reservations are made online or in person; group rooms have specific reservation rules.

cards.title: Choose a quieter floor for focused reading
cards.subtitle: Main Library, upper floors
cards.notes: Use the quiet areas on the third through fifth floors when you need independent reading time, and take calls to the central corridors.
cards.short_summary: Designated quiet seating separates concentrated work from first-floor group activity.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main Library identifies quiet study seating on the third floor and in east and west book-stack areas on the fourth and fifth floors.
cards.source_title: Main Library study spaces and locker information | University of Iowa Libraries
cards.access_notes: Quiet-space guidance permits individual work and asks users to keep conversations quiet.

cards.title: Meet outside with an Old Capitol view
cards.subtitle: South of the Iowa Memorial Union
cards.notes: Plan an outdoor game, information table, or student-organization event here; route organized reservations through IMU Event Services.
cards.short_summary: A campus green used for outdoor activities, fairs, concerts, and social events.
cards.evidence_claim: UI identifies Hubbard Park as the green space south of the IMU and lists outdoor games, social events, student-org fairs, concerts, and information tables as uses.
cards.access_notes: Organized events require coordination with the IMU Event Services Office.

cards.title: Use the fireplace lounge between classes
cards.subtitle: Iowa Memorial Union
cards.notes: Bring reading or a laptop to the fireplace lounge, then use the surrounding IMU tables and Wi-Fi for a low-key study break.
cards.short_summary: A named IMU lounge among the union's shared public spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: The IMU describes studying by the fireplace in Hubbard Commons and identifies the Hubbard Commons fireplace lounge as a shared public space.
cards.access_notes: The IMU lists Wi-Fi, study tables, computer labs, and group-study meeting rooms; some technology access requires a HawkID.

cards.title: Check the public performance calendar
cards.subtitle: 93 E. Burlington Street
cards.notes: Look for a scheduled public performance or presentation, then arrive with time to orient yourself in the downtown music building.
cards.short_summary: The School of Music's downtown building pairs performance spaces with the Rita Benton Music Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The School of Music says Voxman hosts more than 350 yearly public performances and presentations and includes acoustically designed performance and practice spaces.
cards.source_title: Facilities | University of Iowa School of Music
cards.access_notes: The School of Music posts building hours and notes that holiday and academic-break hours differ.

cards.title: See the Writers’ Workshop’s historic home
cards.subtitle: 507 N. Clinton Street
cards.notes: Walk by the historic house and connect its preserved front section with the Iowa Writers’ Workshop that has been based here since 1997.
cards.short_summary: A historic Iowa City house adapted as the home of the Iowa Writers’ Workshop.
cards.evidence_claim: University Facilities identifies Dey House as the Iowa Writers’ Workshop’s home and says the Workshop has occupied it since 1997.
cards.source_title: Dey House | University of Iowa Facilities Management
cards.access_notes: This is an academic building; observe posted access guidance and do not assume interior public access.

cards.title: Explore the landmark at the Pentacrest
cards.subtitle: 21 N. Clinton Street
cards.notes: Use the museum’s visit and calendar information to plan a daytime stop, then connect the building’s Iowa history with the surrounding Pentacrest.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark and University of Iowa museum in the Old Capitol.
cards.evidence_claim: The Old Capitol Museum describes Old Capitol as a National Historic Landmark that welcomes visitors to explore its history.
cards.source_title: Old Capitol Museum | The University of Iowa
cards.access_notes: Check the museum's current hours and visit information before going.

cards.title: Try a recreation activity at the CRWC
cards.subtitle: 309 S. Madison Street
cards.notes: Check current facility access and activity times, then choose from fitness, courts, track, climbing, or aquatic spaces that fit your plan.
cards.short_summary: A large Student Life recreation facility with fitness, climbing, court, track, and pool spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: UI Recreational Services lists fitness space, a climbing wall, pools, a jogging track, basketball and volleyball courts, and a multi-activity gym at the CRWC.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation and Wellness Center | University of Iowa Recreational Services
cards.access_notes: Review current CRWC hours and applicable membership or guest-access requirements before visiting.

cards.title: Visit a community-centered study and gathering space
cards.subtitle: Pride Alliance Center, 601 Melrose Ave.
cards.notes: Check the posted weekday hours, then use the living room, study rooms, games, or computer and printer in this student and community venue.
cards.short_summary: The Pride Alliance Center's house includes social, study, and practical resources.
cards.evidence_claim: UI says Pride House serves students, student organizations, and community members, with study rooms, a living room, computer and printer, games, and a kitchen.
cards.source_title: Facilities | University of Iowa Leadership and Engagement
cards.access_notes: Posted hours are Monday–Thursday 3–9 p.m. and Friday 12–5 p.m.; verify before travel.

cards.title: Use the low-sensory lounge when you need calm
cards.subtitle: University Capitol Centre
cards.notes: Stop by for a lower-sensory place to reset or work, and consult Student Disability Services if you need support or accommodation guidance.
cards.short_summary: An all-student low-sensory study and reset space managed by Student Disability Services.
cards.evidence_claim: University Classrooms identifies the SDS Lounge in University Capitol Centre as a low-sensory space dedicated to students with disabilities and open to all students.
cards.source_title: Student Learning Spaces | University of Iowa
cards.access_notes: Open to all students; confirm building access and any current lounge guidance before visiting.
